detail.reason: Customer reports Salesforce sync bug dropping claim number into wrong field on custom Claim object, plus feature requests for glass intent routing.

assignments.name: Salesforce custom object sync breaks after field changes

steps.summary: Nothing auto-delivered · 1 waiting for a reviewer

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], hey [PERSON_2]. Thanks for making time. I've got [PERSON_3] on with us, she's going to drive the config today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: How's Monday treating you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Busy, but good. We had a spike in claims over the weekend with that storm front, so the timing on this is decent.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, after-hours held up fine, which is kind of why we're here. Ready when you are.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. So the goal today is to take what's working after hours and extend it into daytime overflow. I want to walk the intents, the transfer targets, and then the Salesforce write-back at the end.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Sound okay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Works for us.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Great. Right now the agent is handling claims intake after hours, so FNOL basics, policy lookup, and then a transfer to an on-call adjuster.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: For daytime overflow, which queues should it pick up from?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Start with the general claims line and the policyholder services queue. Those are the two that spill over most days between eleven and two.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. And when the agent can't resolve, where should it hand off?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Same as after hours, the claims queue in Genesys. If nobody's available it should offer a callback rather than hold.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Let's talk intents. After hours we've got FNOL, policy status, and billing. What else do you get during the day that we should cover?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Glass. Glass claims are a big chunk. We need the voice agent to tell a glass claim from a collision claim and send glass straight to our glass vendor's line.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So a separate transfer target for glass, not the claims queue.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right. They have their own intake team. If we route glass into the main claims queue it just bounces back to us and we call the vendor anyway.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: How does the caller describe it usually? Do they say glass, or windshield, or something else?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Windshield, mostly. Sometimes back glass. A few say chip or crack.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, so I'd build a glass signal with those phrases and set the transfer target to the vendor number. I'll need the number and the hours from you, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I'll send it over this afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: And just so we're clear on scope, we're not touching the after-hours flow today. This is a daytime config only.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's fine.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: One thing I want to check before we go further. The agent is passing the caller's digital journey through PreSense on the after-hours flow.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Do you want that on the overflow transfers too?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yes. Our agents lean on that a lot, especially when somebody's been on the site looking at a specific policy.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Now, the write-back. After hours, the call outcome goes to the Case object. Is that still where you want it for overflow?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's the thing. The Salesforce sync is dropping the claim number into the wrong field when it's on our custom Claim object. It works fine on the standard Case object.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. When did you first notice that?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Last week sometime. We caught it doing a spot check on the overnight batch. It's not every record, maybe one in five.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Is it only on the voice agent calls, or are you seeing it from regular tracked calls too?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: As far as I can tell it's specific to the agent calls. The manual ones look fine.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Can you send me a couple of example records? Call ID and the claim number, and I'll take it back to our team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, I'll pull three or four and send them today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Appreciate it. I'm not going to guess at what's happening, we'll get it looked at properly.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: [PERSON_2], do you want to hold the overflow go-live until that's sorted, or run it and reconcile after?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'd rather wait until we know what's going on. [PERSON_1] can still test on his side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Fine by me. I'll run test calls into the glass line once [PERSON_3] has it set up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. And what about the AI Messaging Agent? Do you want the overflow flow to trigger a follow-up text when someone abandons before a transfer?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Let's leave messaging out of this for now. One change at a time.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. So the build is: daytime overflow on two queues, glass intent routed to the vendor, PreSense on, callback offer when no one's available, and the Salesforce write-back stays as-is until we hear back on the claim number issue.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll have the draft config to you by Wednesday, then we can do a test call Thursday if that works.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thursday afternoon is better for me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll send a hold for two o'clock.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: I'll put the notes in the shared doc and flag the Salesforce item so it doesn't get lost. [PERSON_2], [PERSON_1], anything else before we wrap?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Nope, that covers it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: All good. Thanks, both.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Thanks everyone. Talk Thursday.
